title: AzGuard target modular architecture and stabilization contract

sections.title: Scope and evidence baseline
sections.text:
Date: 2026-10-10. Code baseline: `main`, `09612160c98ca6133c894a8f90f5653b9dac6b8f` (0.7.0).
Status: architecture strategy; implementation has not started.

This design fixes the target boundaries, ownership and execution model. The SKM plan records the transition
phases after the target scheme; separate sessions will detail their tasks. This is redistribution of existing
behavior, not a feature expansion.

Inputs: [architecture ideas](../../../../audits/2026-10-09-architecture-modularization.md),
[completed hardening](../../../../audits/2026-10-09-audit.md),
[consistency implementation](../../../../audits/2026-10-09-consistency-design.md),
[roadmap](../../../../ROADMAP.md), [changelog](../../../../CHANGELOG.md), both API manifests and the source code.
The architectural decisions below are based on the current implementation; the earlier document supplies the starting ideas.

Plan state: target architecture recorded; the four required transition phases are skeletons with no executable items. Phase task design is reserved for later sessions.

sections.title: The product we are building
sections.text:
**One small authorization engine, explicit optional modules, independently useful integration packages.**
The engine owns the meaning and safety of an access decision. Modules supply behavior through that meaning;
they do not supply a second engine. Public names and persistent identities belong to these logical boundaries,
not to the directory or Composer archive that currently contains them.

There are three different notions of size:

| Dimension | Target |
|:--|:--|
| What an application must understand | One panel, permission enums, code roles, a subject, grant/revoke and check/authorize. Scopes, journals and extension internals are additional guides. |
| What a basic application executes | The common decision/write path and only its selected sources. No optional-module query, listener, table installation or runtime service resolution. |
| What is distributed | Keep `axiomasoft/azguard` and `axiomasoft/azguard-filament`. Optional AzGuard-only behavior has internal module boundaries; a new Composer package requires an independent purpose. |

The public base can remain open source. A self-contained integration can later have its own distribution and
license. Licensing does not introduce edition switches, alternative decision rules or a second schema into the
engine. Filament is the existing example of such an integration. Internal scopes, audit and generators do not
become separate products merely because they have separate directories.

Lightweight does not mean removing safety. Tenant identity, expiry, consistent authority reads, validation,
fail-closed decisions and one guarded write path are present whenever the corresponding data is used.
Optional modules add no work when inactive; shared reference types and their identity columns remain available.

### Fixed decisions

1. Keep tenant isolation and the tenant/context identity format in core.
2. Put assignment-scope behavior, transactional audit and development generators in separate internal modules.
3. Keep standard source adapters available in the base package, behind source contracts. They are selected explicitly.
4. Keep one scalar decision engine, one query-visibility compiler and one write coordinator.
5. Make plugin contributions panel-specific, typed, deterministic and sealed before requests run.
6. Use core contracts and core values for every module interaction. No sibling imports, dependency on a sibling's
   plugin ID, bridge classes, shared module tables or runtime `class_exists()` integration switches.
7. Freeze the actual consumer and implementer surface, including data formats, rather than a target class count.
8. Complete the module separation before 1.0. Later physical movement must preserve these boundaries and names.

sections.title: Exact ownership and target layout
sections.text:
“Core” is a set of responsibilities inside the base package, not one giant public namespace. Its implementations
are organized by responsibility and hidden behind a small supported surface. Do not manufacture a Composer
package for each core responsibility.

| Responsibility | Owner | What stays there |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Domain values | Core `Kernel` | Permission/role keys, subject/actor/tenant/context references, `AccessScope`, decisions, contribution witnesses and the predicate vocabulary. Pure PHP. |
| Extension language | Core `Contracts/<domain>` | Sources, evaluation inputs, restrictions, conditions, plugin lifecycle, scope evaluation, transactional participation, diagnostics and directories. Only genuinely shared contracts. |
| Declarations and catalogs | Core `Panels`, `Catalog`, `Roles`, `Permissions`, `Policies`, `Schema` | Panel DSL, code permissions/roles, policy declarations, neutral schema descriptors and compiled catalogs. Implementation goes in the owning area's `Internal`. |
| Request context | Core `Context` | Current `AccessScope`, scoped execution, phase/runtime values shared by access, writes and UI. Context carries both tenant and assignment scope; it is not owned by the scopes module. |
| Tenant isolation | Core `Tenancy` | Tenant policy, host tenant definition/resolution, membership enforcement and global-role rules. No tenant or membership database owned by AzGuard. |
| Decision execution | Core `Authorization` | Mandatory stage order, source aggregation, expiry, super-admin rules, policy evaluation, restrictions, batch orchestration and query composition. |
| Authority persistence | Core `Storage`, `Changes` | Six authority tables, revisions/epoch, snapshots, locks, validated changes, effective-change values and commit coordination. No audit table, retention or journal encoding. |
| Standard adapters | Core `Sources/{Database,Folder,Gate,Relation}` | Existing storage, discovery, native Gate and relation-backed sources. Their adapter-specific binding/inspection stays inside the adapter. |
| Host/UI access | Core `Directories`, `Schema` | Subject/tenant directories, lookup contracts and readonly descriptions. Scope-specific directory algorithms are contributed by the scopes module. |
| Framework and operations | Core `Laravel`, `Diagnostics`, `Configuration` | Gate bridge, HTTP/queue lifecycle, doctor/explain, installation, authority maintenance, typed configuration and integration with Laravel's container. |
| Consumer testing | Base package `Testing` | Fake, consumer helpers and contract suites. Suite-only fixtures are internal/test-only, not a public domain API. |
| Assignment scopes | Internal module `AzGuard\Scopes` | Scope definitions' rich configuration, inheritance, role bindings, eligibility, resource mapping, exact query adapters and scope directories/checks. |
| Audit | Internal module `AzGuard\Audit` | Plugin/settings, journal encoding/persistence, audit schema, health checks and retention/prune command. |
| Development tools | Internal module `AzGuard\DevTools` | Generators, scaffolding, stubs and their console provider. Core installation/storage migration remains in core. |
| Filament | `axiomasoft/azguard-filament` | Resource authorization, list filtering, editors, pages, exports and generators for Filament. Uses core API/SPI and neutral descriptors exclusively. |

```text
packages/core/                         axiomasoft/azguard
  src/
    AzGuard.php                       typed application entry point
    AzGuardServiceProvider.php        core composition only
    Facades/AzGuard.php                Laravel adapter to that entry point
    Kernel/                           pure values; final readonly where appropriate
    Contracts/<domain>/               shared extension and consumer contracts
    Context/{Data,Enums,Internal}/
    Tenancy/{Data,Enums,Internal}/
    Panels/ Catalog/ Roles/ Permissions/ Policies/ Schema/
    Authorization/Internal/           pipeline, visibility, batches
    Changes/{Data,Enums,Internal}/
    Storage/{Schema,Models,Internal}/
    Sources/{Database,Folder,Gate,Relation}/
    Directories/ Configuration/ Diagnostics/ Laravel/ Concerns/ Testing/
  database/migrations/                authority installation and upgrades
  modules/
    scopes/src/                       AzGuard\Scopes
      ScopesPlugin.php
      Contracts/ Data/ Enums/ Internal/
    audit/                            AzGuard\Audit
      src/{AuditPlugin.php,AuditServiceProvider.php,Data,Internal}/
      database/migrations/
    devtools/                         AzGuard\DevTools
      src/{DevToolsServiceProvider.php,Internal}/
      stubs/
packages/filament/                     axiomasoft/azguard-filament
```

`Contracts`, `Data`, `Enums`, `Events`, `Exceptions` and `Internal` are ownership categories, not compulsory
empty folders. Keep clear existing public names such as `Panels\PanelBuilder`, `Changes\ChangeResult` and
`Kernel\Identity\SubjectRef`; do not rename them just to fit the diagram. New/shared types use the owning
domain's categories. Move implementation classes into `Internal` while the public wrappers retain their names.
The explicit namespace changes are the mixed `Scopes` responsibilities, audit and generators.

Move `CurrentContext`/`WithinContext` to core `Context`, and tenant policy/definitions to core `Tenancy`.
Move `AssignmentScopePhase`/`AssignmentScopeRuntime` into core context enums/data because writes and UI also use
them. Keep only neutral scope definitions/references in core contracts; richer configurable definitions,
filters and settings belong to the scopes module. Do not leave a core contract returning module-owned settings.

The mutable context store is internal. The supported surface exposes the current context for reading and
validated scoped execution with restoration in `finally`; it does not expose an unchecked `set()` operation.
HTTP, queue and UI adapters enter through that execution boundary. Panel and Fiber locality remain core rules.

`ModelIdentity` currently mixes tenant mapping, context mapping and model keys. Its tenant mapping belongs to
Tenancy; context mapping belongs to the scope evaluator; exact model-key access remains a shared host adapter.
Keep the public `Support\ModelKey` helper. A directory or subject wrapper must not import a scope implementation
to obtain a model's key.

Use explicit PSR-4 mappings for the three module roots; no corresponding `src/Scopes`, `src/Audit` or
`src/DevTools` implementation tree. The package manifest may list providers as distribution metadata. The core
provider must not register modules by importing their classes. Module providers register availability and their
own resources; a panel plugin determines runtime activation. DevTools availability is console-only.

### Dependency map

```mermaid
flowchart BT
    K[Kernel values]
    C[Core contracts and shared data] --> K
    D[Panels and catalogs] --> C
    R[Decision and write coordinators] --> C
    S[Storage and source adapters] --> C
    L[Core Laravel composition] --> D
    L --> R
    L --> S
    SC[Scopes module] --> C
    AU[Audit module] --> C
    DT[DevTools module] --> C
    FI[Filament package] --> C
    FI --> D
```

This is the extension dependency map. Inside core, explicitly owned implementation dependencies are allowed;
Kernel purity and supported-signature closure remain mandatory. Avoid forcing every core service through a new
public interface. The critical prohibitions are core-to-module, sibling-to-sibling and extension-to-internal.

sections.title: The extension system
sections.text:
### Installation, availability, activation, execution

These are separate states. Autoloading makes code installed. A provider makes its services/resources available.
Attaching a plugin activates its declarations for one panel. The engine executes only the compiled contributions
of that panel. Provider discovery must not activate audit or scopes for every panel.

Retain `Plugin::id()`, `register()` and `boot()` as the lifecycle. Registration uses the panel builder as an
explicit declaration API; the compiler records typed contributions, validates them and seals the result.
Module registration performs no database/network I/O and reads no current user, tenant, clock or request.
`boot()` cannot mutate the compiled panel or install global authorization listeners. It is an optional lifecycle
notification after validation, not a second registration route.

Definition descriptors contain scalars, enum values, stable references, validated class strings and immutable
options. Runtime handlers are resolved through Laravel's container for the operation's scope. They are not
cached as request-dependent objects in singleton panel definitions. A readonly runtime input may borrow a host
model; that does not make the model immutable, and such an input is never a cached/serialized definition.

Each panel owns its effective contributions. Preserve explicit list order and the existing documented
provider/plugin/config/default precedence; do not introduce priority sorting that silently changes it.
Duplicate IDs, conflicting providers for a single-valued slot and invalid handler types fail at compilation.
Replacing a required security stage is never an available contribution. An inactive module has no instantiated
runtime handler and does not create tables; disabling it leaves existing data intact.

Built-in modules express compatibility through core capability contracts, not `DependsOnPlugins` IDs.
Retire the ID dependency contract and the corresponding dependency field before the freeze; a plugin may
require a core writer/query capability without identifying which optional module supplies behavior.
Core compatibility validation rejects an audit participant on a writer unable to join its local transaction.
Reserve `azguard/*` IDs through declared ownership, never as a runtime privilege check.

### Supported contribution slots

| Slot | Existing mechanism / target boundary | Authority and failure rule |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Permission/role/source declarations | Existing catalogs and `Contracts/Sources/*` | Supply definitions or candidates; core validates panel, tenant, context, origin, expiry and provenance. A source cannot emit a final allow. |
| Before hooks | Existing before stage; typed continue/deny result | Can veto or continue. Cannot skip Boundary or create authority. |
| Policies | Existing explicit policy/Gate declarations | Core preserves the current authority modes and evaluates policy outcomes in the mandatory pipeline. |
| Restrictions and grant conditions | Existing `Restriction`, `GrantCondition` | May narrow authority. Exceptions become failure, never an allow or silently absent restriction. |
| Exact query support | Existing `FiltersAccessQueries`, contribution witnesses and core query guards | Core owns final grouping/tenant guards. Unsupported equivalence produces explicit unsupported/failure behavior; it never broadens a list. |
| Assignment-scope behavior | Core `Contracts/Scopes/AssignmentScopeEvaluator` plus optional `QueryableAssignmentScopeEvaluator` | One cohesive evaluator for resolution, applicability, admission, resource mapping and neutral descriptions; optional exact query capability shares its semantics. Neither returns a final `Decision`. |
| Change transformation/validation | Existing `changing`, made an explicit `ChangePipe` SPI | Final validation remains in core; continuation runs once and the writer's result cannot be replaced. Cancellation throws and rolls back. |
| Transactional effective-change participation | Core `Contracts/Changes/ChangeParticipant` | Receives immutable effective-change/event values after the writer, before root commit, and a restricted module-table transaction capability. Error rolls back the operation. |
| Post-decision observation | Existing after stage / access event | Observe the produced result. No replacement or retrospective authorization. |
| Public change notification | Existing `AccessEvent` hierarchy | Dispatch after root commit; rollback/retry publishes no discarded attempt. Public delivery remains best effort. |
| UI descriptions and lookups | Existing schema/directory contracts and DTOs | Core delegates scope descriptions/lookups to the evaluator's contributions. UI always revalidates the final write. |
| Diagnostics | Existing `DoctorCheck`, source `ChecksHealth`, plugin `doctorChecks()` | Checks are owned by the relevant source/module; the doctor only aggregates typed findings. |

No macros on the supported authorization, panel, change or query API. No untyped extension-option bag,
arbitrary stage insertion, module event bus or dynamic methods to impersonate a core capability.
Laravel facades remain a convenience adapter; the same operations have real typed methods on `AzGuard\AzGuard`.

Core configuration owns storage, host-key formats, panels, sources, framework wiring and consistency limits.
Scope filters/bindings, audit retention and generator destinations are owned by their module's typed options.
The compiler sees their neutral descriptors and fingerprint inputs, not a general options array it interprets.
Keep one documented precedence order and reject unknown options. Configuration defaults must not resolve an
inactive module or make two panels share one mutable options object.

### Scope evaluator: one implementation, several callers

The core evaluator contract owns the neutral question “does this contribution apply in this access scope?”
The scopes module owns inheritance, configured filters, model definitions and role-binding algorithms.
The same evaluator is called by scalar access, batch preparation, write admission, resource mapping and scope
directories. Assignment, access, revocation and inspection remain distinct phases; listing eligible assignments
must use the same assignment rules as the write.

The default core implementation accepts only the global assignment scope. It does not accept a non-global
request, silently globalize an existing grant or ignore a role's required scope. Missing required scope behavior
is a configuration error or a fail-closed outcome. No data is deleted when the module is disabled.
Tenant ownership and reference/model identity are checked by core around evaluator results; a module's positive
answer cannot override a tenant mismatch. Membership/inheritance-specific narrowing belongs to the evaluator.

Exact SQL support is a separate capability, so an external scope can support scalar access without pretending
to have an exact list predicate. Reuse the existing predicate/guarded-query mechanisms. A scope query adapter
works on an isolated candidate query, can only narrow its predicates, and cannot alter or execute the outer
resource query. Core validates model/connection identity and owns contribution-bound OR branches and mandatory
AND guards. Do not assume every existing scope query can be represented by a new simplified predicate DSL.

Do not store the evaluator as an application-wide binding overwritten by whichever panel boots last.
It is a typed contribution of the compiled panel, resolved with that panel's immutable options.

### Authority reads: keep the database mechanism deep

Put snapshot acquisition, physical-handle grouping, raw row materialization and cache publication behind one
internal authority-read coordinator. `ReadAttempt`, `ReadSessions` and the database adapter already contain the
mechanism to redistribute. The decision stages consume materialized values and observed evidence, not PDOs or
database row-hydration helpers.

Keep `FencesReads` for independently versioned sources and its bounded retry of materialization only. Database
snapshots, subject revisions, epochs and after-commit cache publication remain implementation details of the
database coordinator. Do not replace each concrete-source branch with a separate public capability interface.
Move live automatic-role handling into catalog/source preparation; decision semantics must not depend on an
`instanceof FolderSource`. Source binding/catalog validation becomes a coherent source lifecycle capability,
implemented by the relevant adapters, rather than `instanceof RelationSource` in the panel compiler.

Snapshot scope is the physical database handle; logical stores retain distinct prefixes and cache namespaces.
There is no global snapshot promise across unrelated databases or external services. Handler/policy execution
does not repeat because an authority read retries, and pinned handles close before observers retain a frame.

sections.title: How the complete operation chains work
sections.text:
### Building a panel

```text
typed package config + panel provider + explicitly attached plugins
  -> ordered declarations and immutable module options
  -> core contract/type/conflict/compatibility validation
  -> selected source preparation and catalog compilation
  -> neutral schema/directory contributions + configuration fingerprints
  -> sealed panel definition
  -> request/job-scoped handler resolution when an operation needs it
```

Scope definitions contribute stable aliases and descriptors; rich module settings do not leak into core
catalog code. Fingerprinting includes effective module options, scope bindings and handler identities through
core metadata. Cached definitions never retain container services, closures' execution state or Eloquent
models. A code/namespace change invalidates disposable catalogs and caches, not persisted grant identities.

### Checking one permission

```text
typed API / model helper / Gate / middleware / Filament
  -> select panel, subject and explicit/current AccessScope
  -> Prepare: capture time and host inputs
  -> Boundary: validate identities and tenant boundary; ask scope evaluator
  -> Before: veto/continue
  -> materialize authority once through the read coordinator
  -> Authority: code modes, grants, roles, super-admin and policy rules
  -> Restriction: scope applicability, restrictions and grant conditions
  -> immutable allow / deny / failed / not-applicable result
  -> After / explain / optional notification
```

These are logical responsibilities, not a new stage order: keep the existing
`Prepare -> Boundary -> Before -> Authority -> Restriction -> After` graph and its tested evaluation timing.
The scope evaluator is invoked at the relevant existing boundary/qualification points. Modules cannot remove
tenant checks, policy vetoes, expiry or restrictions. Infrastructure/contract failures remain distinguishable
from ordinary denial, including the existing HTTP responder mapping.

### Batch and visible lists

`DecisionSet` prepares inputs once and shares authority snapshots by physical handle, retaining each supplied
subject model. Each decision then follows the same rules as a scalar check. Keep the subject cap and fail as a
set when its required snapshot cannot be established; do not silently chunk it into different authority states.

`visibleTo()` uses the same permission modes, contribution witnesses, scope evaluator and captured time.
Its core compiler combines each qualified grant alternative inside its own OR branch and then applies mandatory
guards. SQL NULL behavior is explicit. Unsupported adapters are reported; row-by-row filtering after pagination
and approximate predicates are not substitutes for exact visibility. Filament delegates to this path.

### Changing grants and writing audit

```text
host-authorized grant/revoke/sync/update operation
  -> core writer coordinator: panel lock + local transaction
  -> fresh locked reads, captured time and actor; tenant/scope/field validation
  -> typed ChangePipe sequence, guarded continuation and final core validation
  -> writer applies changes and produces immutable effects
  -> core builds the corresponding event values once
  -> active ChangeParticipants receive effects/events in that transaction
       Audit: writes its own table using those exact event IDs and payloads
  -> root commit updates authority state and makes the effects durable
  -> publish those events and eligible cache entries after commit
```

Audit is a transactional participant, not an after-commit listener that reconstructs rows. One effective change
has one journal row; a no-op has none. Rollback, nested rollback and retried attempts leave neither durable rows
nor published events from discarded work. A journal failure fails the audited change. Public listener failure
does not undo a committed grant. External durable delivery/outbox is outside this redistribution.

`ChangeEventPublisher` stays internal. Split its event-value construction from dispatch; participants receive
core-built values rather than importing the publisher or independently generating event IDs. `ChangeJournal`
row encoding and persistence move to Audit. Pruning is Audit-owned and does not raise authorization revisions.
Capture effective retention in the panel's module options; pruning must not inspect `PanelRecipe` internals.

Do not publish the complete `StorageMutation`. Its table access, `touch`, state/lifecycle methods and callbacks
are too broad for the module boundary. Expose a restricted module-table mutation capability under core change
contracts: current operation's connection/transaction, declared owned tables and lifetime only. It provides no
direct authority-table write, lock replacement, epoch mutation, commit/close or arbitrary connection selection.
The module's own table names and row mapping remain module-owned. This prevents accidental invariant bypass;
in-process extension PHP remains trusted code, not sandboxed code.

The capability must not return a raw connection or unrestricted query builder that defeats its table boundary.
Audit needs bounded insertion of validated rows for the active change, not a new generic storage repository SPI.
Its installation/health paths consume a readonly storage descriptor (selected connection, prefix and host-key
format) and the shared identity-column helper. Its retention path uses its own module-owned transaction;
neither path receives authority state mutation or a core coordinator.

### Filament and tools

Filament consumes core panel access, decisions, schema descriptors and directories. A scope editor is rendered
from contributed core descriptors, not a check for `azguard/scopes` or an import of `ScopesPlugin`. It cannot
derive a separate eligibility rule or bypass validation when the user submits a chosen ID.

DevTools owns generated code/templates, but the output uses supported API/SPI. A module-specific generator
belongs to that module. Core install/storage migration commands do not import DevTools or its stub storage.
Use an explicit output target when installation scaffolding is requested; installing core must also work
without any generator services.

sections.title: Persistence: freeze meaning and ownership
sections.text:
Keep schema version 2's authority structure. The redistribution needs **no grant/identity data migration**.
There is no justification here for renamed columns, separate tenant joins or another set of grant tables.

| Persistent object | Final owner | Extraction/redistribution rule |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `{prefix}permissions` | Core storage | Preserve panel + tenant + permission identity, metadata and host-field behavior. |
| `{prefix}role_grants`, `{prefix}permission_grants` | Core storage | Preserve tenant/subject/context/origin identity and uniqueness, expiry, actor fields and application columns. Scope behavior moves; the grant format does not. |
| `{prefix}panel_state`, `{prefix}subject_revisions` | Core storage | Preserve incarnation, version, epoch and subject-revision semantics; no module writes these tables. |
| `{prefix}storage_state` | Core storage | Preserve schema/codec/storage ID/prefix/host-key descriptor. A module does not write its version into this row. |
| `{prefix}audit_log` | Audit module | Preserve the existing name, columns, indexes, constraints, event IDs and historical payloads. Move installation, health checking, insertion and pruning together. |
| Tenant/scope models and membership | Host application | Scopes/Tenancy resolve through contracts and stable aliases. No new AzGuard table. |
| Scope, DevTools and Filament persistence | None | These units currently need no AzGuard-owned table; redistribution adds none for them. |

`tenant_*` and `context_*` remain core identity fields even when a module is inactive. `context_key = global`
means tenant-wide applicability, not a global tenant. Pair constraints preserve the null/global form; they do
not imply that disabling a module converts existing scoped rows to global rows.

Freeze the following together: morph/type aliases, role/permission keys, source `origin` labels,
`IdentityCodec::VERSION`, the `global` sentinel, host-key canonicalization, lengths, byte/collation semantics,
UTC timestamps, ULID event IDs, event type strings and audit payload shapes. Moving a PHP class changes none of
these identities. A host class rename requires the same stable alias, not rewriting every grant.

### Audit installation and adoption

On a fresh installation, core creates six authority tables. Audit publishes its own migration only when the
application chooses audit; merely discovering its provider does not migrate its table. Module schema helpers
use the selected core storage's connection, prefix and host-key types, including additional named storages.
Expose shared identity-column/constraint construction through a small schema helper; keep database coordinators
and broad storage mutation private.

On a 0.7.0 database, adopt the existing audit table in place after checking its full shape. `hasTable()` alone is
not evidence of compatibility. Preserve every row and migration basename. An adoption migration's rollback
must not delete a table it merely adopted; audit data is retained by default. Core teardown no longer owns the
audit table. Document the intentional pre-1.0 installer/teardown change rather than disguising it as file movement.

The existing migration files delegate to `StorageSchema::create/drop/upgrade`; preserving filenames alone does
not freeze their effective behavior. The redistribution must qualify fresh installation, existing schema-2
adoption, schema-1 upgrade and published application migrations. Keep the existing version/history rather than
squashing it on the assumption that nobody installed 0.7.0.

After 1.0, extraction itself performs no DDL or row rewrite. New functionality may own a new table through a
new migration, but cannot alter core or another module's table. Normal compatible schema evolution uses new
additive migrations; changing stored meaning/types/identities is a major-version operation. Reserve `azg_`
field names now alongside existing identity prefixes to avoid future collisions with application grant fields.
`meta` remains application grant data, not a module-to-module mailbox. Avoid cross-owner foreign keys.

Disposable catalog/permission caches are separate from durable data: invalidate/rebuild them on changed class
metadata. Never treat serialized runtime objects or class names in those caches as the persistent identity contract.

sections.title: What exactly becomes stable
sections.text:
| Surface | Decision before 1.0 |
|:--|:--|
| Real application API | Replace the internal manager-shaped entry point with typed `AzGuard\AzGuard`; facade signatures mirror it. Keep established model helpers and panel access. No new implicit panel or wholesale helper renaming in this redistribution. |
| Consume vs implement/extend | Classify explicitly. `BaseRole`, `PanelProvider`, plugin bases and extension interfaces need implementer/subclass promises, not only consumer promises. |
| Types and members | Supported publication is explicit; `Internal` and member-level internal factories/helpers are excluded. No automatic publication of every exception/schema/kernel/testing type by directory. |
| Shared DTO placement | Keep clear domain names; move only mixed/module-owned dependencies out of shared signatures. No generic `Contracts/Values` dumping ground and no interface for each concrete DTO/service. |
| Helpers and constructors | Pure Kernel helpers such as `Kernel\Support\Narrow` remain internal unless there is a demonstrated supported use. A module must use supported constructors/validation instead of importing a helper solely because it is under Kernel. |
| State evidence | Make both database/code tokens opaque public observations; hide storage counters and raw read-session details. Freeze a versioned serialization and equality contract; do not offer ordering or replica-wait semantics. Keep historical audit payloads readable without rewriting them. |
| Decisions | Retain typed readonly outcome values and contribution lists. Classify HTTP-response details as deliberate Laravel adapter compatibility, not inputs that a module can use to create authority. |
| Closed vocabularies | Enum public finite modes/operations, including stringly typed tenant/scope modes and predicate operations. Keep intentional wire values such as `context_*`; document the assignment-scope/context terminology mapping. |
| Errors | Keep useful typed domain exceptions and stable codes. No removal of meaningful `catch` targets to satisfy a numerical API budget. |
| Scope/module declarations | Scope policy DSL is on `ScopesPlugin`; core exposes the typed evaluator contribution slot. Module implementations/configurable settings do not occur in core API/SPI signatures. |
| Config and commands | Freeze keys, types, defaults, precedence, environment names, command options/exit codes and publish tags. Remove the single-choice `GateMode` setting in the same pre-1.0 transition; keep the existing explicit consistency controls. |
| Events and machine output | Freeze event types/envelopes, doctor finding IDs/severities/JSON and explain JSON. Retain the deliberate public `PanelStateTouched` fact; internal cache invalidation messages stay internal. |
| Models and testing | Keep supported host customization of grant models/helpers and the consumer fake/suites. Internal Eloquent/read-session APIs and suite fixtures are not general extension contracts. |

The current manifest publishes 247 core types (206 API, 41 SPI) and 21 Filament types. This is a baseline,
not the desired count. Its 97 unmarked location-published core types need explicit ownership/classification;
closing a factory is often more useful than removing an entire class.

The generator must describe the real facade/service surface, public constant values, supported protected
override points, PHPDoc generic/class-string contracts and supported member factories. It currently records
zero facade methods and also records 59 core public methods documented as internal. A regenerated manifest is
a consistency check; compatibility requires comparison against a frozen release baseline as well.

Do the necessary namespace, DSL, token, typing and publication changes as **one documented pre-1.0 contract
transition**, implemented in several safe steps. Supply one coherent upgrade map from 0.7.0 and update the
existing legacy upgrade examples. After that candidate baseline, change only what qualification demonstrates
is necessary. Do not keep reopening naming and API shape while approaching the release.

sections.title: Transition policy and conditional physical extraction
sections.text:
The target scheme is recorded first; the plan then carries four ordered skeleton phases: schema/security, API/SPI, consolidation/module movement and candidate qualification/freeze. Their goals, boundaries, approximate sizes, compatibility effects and checkable exits are in the phase records. Later sessions detail one phase at a time; no implementation item is authored or executed in this design session.

### Conditional future phase E

Physical extraction is outside the required 1.0 phases. Open a follow-on plan only for a demonstrated independent integration/adapter purpose. AzGuard-only modules stay internal. An extraction rehearsal must preserve FQCNs, configuration/command/event identities, migration history, populated data and one autoload owner; it must document Composer dependency/distribution compatibility. Moving existing code alone needs no schema or data migration. Separate licensing cannot introduce a second engine or schema.

### Artifacts to author during phase detail

Keep one owner for each artifact: table/format ownership and driver fixtures; API/SPI type/member/override inventory; extension semantics; namespace/DSL/config upgrade map; module activation/dependency matrix; cache/fingerprint contract; scalar/batch/query/write/directory parity fixtures; transactional/race/load evidence; candidate and stable-tag baselines. `api-manifest.json` remains generated and DDL fixtures come from actual drivers. Reuse existing tests and contract suites.

Do not add implicit panels, consistency profiles, subject-level write locks, a replica freshness receipt, distributed transactions, external audit delivery or a general plugin workflow engine to this transition. Those retain their existing roadmap status.

sections.title: Release gate and permanent architecture rules
sections.text:
1.0 is released only when all of the following are true on the candidate commit:

1. **Small core demonstrated:** a basic consumer uses only the base API. Scopes and Audit are inactive by default;
   DevTools is console-only. Core-only boot/check/write needs no module runtime service, module query or module
   table. Filament is an optional Composer dependency and is absent from core requirements.
2. **Boundaries complete:** core has no module imports, module table names or plugin-ID conditionals; modules
   have no sibling/bridge dependency. Filament and modules use supported core symbols and neutral descriptors.
   Every production file, including root providers and the typed API, has one owner.
3. **Supported surface closed:** API/SPI types, members, inheritance/override points and facade operations are
   explicitly classified. Signatures and documented generic types contain no module/internal leakage. Manifest
   checks are green without exemptions hiding an unresolved module boundary.
4. **Extension semantics proved:** real built-ins and an independent consumer fixture use the same slots.
   Invalid contributions, double/skipped continuation, forged writer results, duplicate IDs and incompatible
   writers fail safely. A contribution cannot bypass core validation through the supported API.
5. **Persistence frozen:** actual DDL/constraints/collations/host keys match fixtures on SQLite, PostgreSQL,
   MySQL and MariaDB. Fresh/core+module installs, adoption, existing application migrations and rollback/data
   retention are qualified. Relocating module code requires no grant, identity or audit-row rewrite.
6. **Behavior conserved:** scalar, batch, visibility, directory and write-admission results agree for supported
   mappings, including expiry, NULL, tenant ownership, global/scoped roles and retained subject-model instances.
   Missing/unsupported capabilities fail closed and remain diagnosable.
7. **Consistency conserved:** snapshot/race, dirty-read rejection, nested rollback, retry, after-commit/cache and
   handle-release suites pass. Repeat recorded load/query-budget profiles on the changed paths; no unexpected
   mixed-state decision or unbounded per-subject SQL regression is accepted.
8. **Non-PHP contracts frozen:** config/defaults, environment names, identities/codecs, event/audit formats,
   exception codes, commands/options/exit codes, publish tags, doctor/explain JSON and HTTP mapping have fixtures
   and documentation. Historical 0.7.0 audit payloads remain usable if token serialization changes.
9. **Distribution qualified:** supported PHP/Laravel and database/cache/replica suites, static/style/type/coverage
   and docs gates pass. Core and core+Filament built archives work in clean applications; consumer checks are
   blocking. Release qualification cannot bypass those checks on a tag.
10. **Freeze operational:** one upgrade map covers the planned break; a candidate/final tag is the compatibility
    baseline. After 1.0, CI compares against the previous stable tag, not merely regenerated files in the PR.
    Adding methods to implementer interfaces or abstract bases, renaming parameters used by named arguments,
    altering defaults and extending exhaustively matched enums are compatibility decisions, not automatic additions.

### CI rules

| Rule | Enforcement / existing foundation |
|:--|:--|
| Complete ownership | Scan every production/autoload root, not only a handwritten list of namespaces. Reject unowned types and duplicate FQCNs. |
| Kernel purity | Retain `ZonesArchTest` plus framework-helper scan; include new roots in forbidden dependencies. |
| Core/module and sibling isolation | Resolve imports, aliases, grouped imports, FQCNs, registration class strings and documented signature types. Reject module imports and module-specific literals in core runtime. Distribution metadata is explicitly separate. |
| Supported-symbol/member usage | Extend `ApiManifestTest` to internal modules and generated stubs; check referenced members as well as class presence. Scan inherited/overridable surfaces and facade/service signatures. |
| Read/write ownership | Only core coordinators use authority tables and internal sessions/mutations; modules access their owned tables through the restricted capability. Preserve direct-write guards. |
| Activation isolation | Test no optional I/O/table creation with inactive modules; test core plus each module and their combinations, including different options on two panels. |
| Sealed definitions and lifecycle | Test deterministic contributions/fingerprints, conflict rejection, request/job/Fiber context restoration and no singleton current-panel leakage. |
| One decision semantics | Maintain property/parity tests for scalar/batch/SQL and eligibility/write/directory paths, including unsupported adapters and failure taxonomy. |
| Transactional audit | Exercise no-op, rollback, nested changes/retry, event-ID equality and root-commit publication; listener failures never impersonate durable journaling. |
| Schema and format compatibility | Driver DDL fixtures plus populated upgrade/adoption fixtures; stable wire/config/CLI snapshots. Changes need a new migration or an intentional major-version contract change. |
| Consumer/distribution safety | Make the existing archive fixture mandatory; exercise optimized autoload, configuration/catalog caching and module isolation. Preserve package version routing and generated manifest checks. |
| Post-1.0 compatibility | Compare supported API/SPI and machine/persistent formats to the stable tag; no baseline update in a PR can silently legalize a break. |

sections.title: Code anchors and patterns used
sections.text:
These anchors identify what is redistributed and which existing mechanisms must survive. They are evidence
for the design, not a separate review backlog.

| Area | Current implementation and implication |
|:--|:--|
| Publication | [manifest generator](../../../../bin/api-manifest.php), [API architecture test](../../../../tests/Arch/ApiManifestTest.php), [facade](../../../../packages/core/src/Facades/AzGuard.php), [manager](../../../../packages/core/src/AzGuardManager.php): facade methods/member contracts need real coverage. |
| Plugin lifecycle | [Plugin](../../../../packages/core/src/Contracts/Plugins/Plugin.php), [PanelCompiler](../../../../packages/core/src/Panels/PanelCompiler.php), [PanelRecipe](../../../../packages/core/src/Panels/PanelRecipe.php), [PanelFingerprint](../../../../packages/core/src/Panels/PanelFingerprint.php): retain per-panel copies, sealing and precedence; make contribution ownership explicit. |
| Scope sharing | [ScopeEligibility](../../../../packages/core/src/Authorization/ScopeEligibility.php), [VisibilityScope](../../../../packages/core/src/Authorization/Query/VisibilityScope.php), [ChangeValidator](../../../../packages/core/src/Changes/ChangeValidator.php), [QueryScopeDirectory](../../../../packages/core/src/Directories/QueryScopeDirectory.php): these callers must share evaluator semantics, not copy algorithms. |
| Hidden scope dependencies | [RoleCompiler](../../../../packages/core/src/Catalog/RoleCompiler.php), [SchemaBuilder](../../../../packages/core/src/Schema/SchemaBuilder.php), [DirectoryResolver](../../../../packages/core/src/Directories/DirectoryResolver.php), [ConfigurableAssignmentScopeDefinition](../../../../packages/core/src/Contracts/Scopes/ConfigurableAssignmentScopeDefinition.php): registration, settings and UI lookup defaults must move with the behavior. |
| Context/host identity | [CurrentContext](../../../../packages/core/src/Scopes/CurrentContext.php), [WithinContext](../../../../packages/core/src/Scopes/WithinContext.php), [ModelIdentity](../../../../packages/core/src/Scopes/ModelIdentity.php), [ModelKey](../../../../packages/core/src/Support/ModelKey.php): preserve panel/Fiber locality and exact keys while separating ownership. |
| Source integration | [ReadAttempt](../../../../packages/core/src/Authorization/ReadAttempt.php), [ReadSessions](../../../../packages/core/src/Authorization/ReadSessions.php), [PanelSources](../../../../packages/core/src/Sources/PanelSources.php), [PanelRegistry](../../../../packages/core/src/Panels/PanelRegistry.php): hide database/source preparation mechanics behind coherent coordinators. |
| Snapshot behavior | [StorageReadSession](../../../../packages/core/src/Storage/StorageReadSession.php), [FencesReads](../../../../packages/core/src/Contracts/Sources/FencesReads.php), [DecisionSetSnapshotTest](../../../../tests/Feature/Authorization/Batch/DecisionSetSnapshotTest.php), [ReadSessionLifecycleTest](../../../../tests/Feature/Authorization/Batch/ReadSessionLifecycleTest.php): physical-handle grouping and timely release are hard constraints. |
| Journal coupling | [RecordChange](../../../../packages/core/src/Plugins/Audit/RecordChange.php), [ChangeJournal](../../../../packages/core/src/Changes/ChangeJournal.php), [ChangePipeline](../../../../packages/core/src/Changes/ChangePipeline.php), [ChangeEventPublisher](../../../../packages/core/src/Changes/ChangeEventPublisher.php), [DatabaseSource](../../../../packages/core/src/Sources/Database/DatabaseSource.php): event construction, active mutation, insertion and pruning currently cross the intended Audit boundary. |
| Mutation safety | [StorageMutation](../../../../packages/core/src/Storage/StorageMutation.php), [OnceTerminal](../../../../packages/core/src/Changes/OnceTerminal.php): preserve the guarded terminal; expose only module-owned table participation. |
| Data ownership | [StorageSchema](../../../../packages/core/src/Storage/Schema/StorageSchema.php), [HostKeyColumns](../../../../packages/core/src/Storage/Schema/HostKeyColumns.php), [StorageHealth](../../../../packages/core/src/Sources/Database/StorageHealth.php), [migration files](../../../../packages/core/database/migrations): move all audit ownership, not only the plugin. |
| Existing schema evidence | [DdlSnapshot](../../../../tests/Fixtures/Storage/DdlSnapshot.php), [StorageSchemaTest](../../../../tests/Feature/Storage/StorageSchemaTest.php), [StorageDdlTest](../../../../tests/Engines/StorageDdlTest.php): extend existing real-driver fixtures to separate core/module installation and adoption. |
| Persisted/API values | [IdentityCodec](../../../../packages/core/src/Kernel/Identity/IdentityCodec.php), [StateToken](../../../../packages/core/src/Kernel/Decision/StateToken.php), [AccessEvent](../../../../packages/core/src/Events/AccessEvent.php), [Field](../../../../packages/core/src/Schema/Field.php): codecs, wire tokens and reserved field names are part of the freeze. |
| Adapter composition | [core provider](../../../../packages/core/src/AzGuardServiceProvider.php), [InstallCommand](../../../../packages/core/src/Laravel/Console/Commands/InstallCommand.php), [AuditPruneCommand](../../../../packages/core/src/Laravel/Console/Commands/AuditPruneCommand.php), [Filament GrantEditor](../../../../packages/filament/src/Editors/GrantEditor.php): remove optional implementation knowledge from core/UI orchestration. |
| Consumer gate | [tests workflow](../../../../.github/workflows/tests.yml), [release workflow](../../../../.github/workflows/release.yml), [consumer fixture](../../../../bin/consumer-fixture.sh): archive qualification becomes blocking and is required before splitting a release. |

### Ecosystem alignment

Apply [ADR 0001](../../../../docs/adr/0001-ecosystem-conventions.md): readonly typed configuration, actor/ref semantics,
stable morph aliases, after-commit envelopes, condition-specific errors, command conventions and consumer suites.
Keep AzGuard's own domain vocabulary and do not add a runtime dependency on another ecosystem package merely
to share style.

Local source samples inspected: CoreX `586012eb6fe5` (`Modules/Contracts/ModuleRegistrar.php` and its internal
provider adapter); Chatom `fb33a54f0d74` (`Plugins/Contracts/Plugin.php` and architecture structure);
Commerz `5e788787d5d7` (`Plugins/Contracts/CommerzPlugin.php`, typed config and core ports);
Vaulter `57d6164e9c7d` (`Configuration/TenancyConfig.php`). Transfer the common practices: explicit contracts,
domain-owned data, hidden implementations, typed options and a small composition root. Package counts and
product-specific sibling dependencies are not templates for AzGuard.

### External precedents

Primary sources were checked on 2026-10-10, with Perplexity used to locate patterns. Their applications below
are design inferences for AzGuard; none is a proposal to add a runtime dependency.

| Precedent | Applied principle |
|:--|:--|
| [Symfony Contracts](https://symfony.com/doc/current/components/contracts.html#design-principles) | Contracts are small domain sets with proven implementations and reference semantics/tests. Keep AzGuard contracts internal to the product until independent use exists. |
| [Symfony service tags](https://symfony.com/doc/current/service_container/tags.html) | Collect and validate contributions before execution. Adapt the pattern to the existing Laravel panel compiler. |
| [Laravel Pipeline implementation](https://github.com/laravel/framework/blob/12.x/src/Illuminate/Pipeline/Pipeline.php) | A pipe can short-circuit; core-owned wrappers and the existing guarded continuation are necessary for security/write invariants. |
| [Laravel after-transaction events](https://laravel.com/docs/13.x/events#dispatching-events-after-database-transactions) | Public notifications follow commit; same-transaction audit participation is a different contract. |
| [Laravel package development](https://laravel.com/docs/13.x/packages), [Spatie package tools](https://github.com/spatie/laravel-package-tools/blob/main/README.md) | Providers/resources can have separate installation boundaries without one Composer package per feature. Installation does not equal activation. |
| [Spatie permission teams](https://spatie.be/docs/laravel-permission/v8/basic-usage/teams-permissions) | Team identity affects assignment semantics and migrations. Keep AzGuard identity columns invariant instead of tying them to module installation. |
| [Spatie activitylog installation](https://spatie.be/docs/laravel-activitylog/v5/installation-and-setup) | Audit persistence can own its table and installation. AzGuard additionally preserves its existing same-transaction guarantee. |
| [Composer schema/autoload](https://getcomposer.org/doc/04-schema.md#autoload) | Preserve logical FQCNs while changing autoload/distribution ownership; test archives and single ownership explicitly. |

Validation for this document: repository/source/manifests and existing test definitions inspected;
`php bin/api-manifest.php --check` passed. Existing audit/bench results are historical evidence, not a new full
qualification run. No implementation or database mutation was performed.

Plan-format validation: `plan.py check` returned 0 errors and 0 warnings; `plan.py render --check` confirmed current human views. All 59 local design links and the recorded repository decision anchors were checked for existence. The four phases remain skeletons with no task items or execution results. These are artifact checks, not a 1.0 qualification run.
